data.name: Chitrani
data.gender_notes: Chitrani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'chitra' which means 'picture' or 'image'. In Hindu mythology, Chitrani is the name of a goddess of beauty and creativity. The name Chitrani carries the meaning “Picture, Image, Beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitrani usually hope their child will grow to embody picture, image, beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner beauty and artistic expression of an individual.
data.etymology: Chitrani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Picture, Image, Beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitrani total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chitrani is associated with the arts and creativity in Hindu culture. It is believed that individuals with this name possess a natural ability to create beautiful and inspiring works of art, be it through painting, literature, music, or any other form of expression. This name is a source of pride for those who bear it, as it represents the rich artistic heritage of Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Chitrani is also considered a manifestation of the divine goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, music, and arts. For Hindus, the name Chitrani is a reminder of the divine creative force that exists within each of us and encourages us to use our gifts to create beauty and inspire others. It also reminds us to use our creative abilities to seek knowledge and wisdom, and to serve and uplift others through our art and expression.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chitrani: The radiant one, adorned with the beautiful paintings of life. Her name symbolizes the artistic expression of the soul, as she delicately weaves the intricacies of existence with grace and creativity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Chitrani was a courtesan in the 16th century in the Vijayanagara Empire. The name Chitrani carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Chitrani was a renowned courtesan in the royal court of the Vijayanagara Empire. She was known for her beauty and her artistic talents, particularly in music and dance.
